assessment.title: CARSI Building Science Foundations — Applied task: read the building and the air on one job
assessment.instructions:
## Applied task

Use a real job you have worked on, or the supplied job. **State whether your job is in Australia or New Zealand, and apply that country's rules.**

**Supplied job:** a 1990s brick-veneer house in Brisbane in February (or, if you work in New Zealand, a 1970s timber house with a suspended floor in a town of your choice). A flexible hose has wet a bedroom (3.6 m × 3.2 m × 2.4 m) and its timber floor. On day two the bedroom reads 25 °C and 75 %RH, an unaffected room reads 24 °C and 55 %RH, and outside reads 26.3 °C and 66 %RH. A dehumidifier inlet reads 25 °C and 70 %RH and its outlet 33 °C and 25 %RH; its stated airflow is 350 m³/h. The owner runs the air conditioner at 21 °C at night and reports a musty smell behind the external wall.

Submit one PDF, or a set of photos and documents, containing:

1. **The four numbers.** For every reading point, calculate vapour pressure, g/kg and dew point at 1013.25 hPa (or your station pressure), showing each step.
2. **Evaporation and the lever.** For the wet floor, calculate the vapour pressure difference now, and after each lever (warming the floor, drying the air). Say which lever you would use and why.
3. **Materials and the dry standard.** Describe how you would set the dry standard for the floor from unaffected material, with the meter and setting recorded. Do not quote a universal moisture percentage.
4. **Condensation and ventilation.** Run the surface condensation check for the external wall in the air-conditioned case, and decide whether to ventilate from a g/kg comparison. Name the NCC climate zone (or, in New Zealand, the Building Code clause that applies) and state what you would refer to a builder or certifier.
5. **Monitoring and the report.** Calculate the dehumidifier depression and an estimate of litres per hour, set out a three-visit log, and write a one-paragraph owner summary that separates moisture findings from any mould question.

Use Australian English and metric units throughout, with power at 230 V. Name any standard by title only; do not copy text from any standard.

criteria.criterion: Four numbers calculated correctly with working shown, at a stated pressure
Vapour pressure difference calculated for both levers and the choice justified
Dry standard set from unaffected same material, meter and setting recorded, no universal target
Condensation check and ventilation decision argued in g/kg, with the correct AU or NZ rule and referral
Depression and litres estimate correct; log and owner summary keep moisture and mould findings separate
